question: In the Indian subcontinent, the beginning of settlement at Mehrgarh started about __________ years ago.
solution:
The correct answer is __**8000**__ years ago.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mehrgarh is one of the earliest known settlements in the Indian subcontinent, dating back to around 8000 years ago.
 
• It is located in present-day Pakistan, in the Balochistan province.
 
• The settlement is significant for its early evidence of farming (wheat and barley) and herding (cattle, sheep, and goats).
 
• Mehrgarh is considered a precursor to the Indus Valley Civilization, showcasing early human advancements in agriculture and settlement patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mehrgarh**

 
 
• Mehrgarh is one of the most important Neolithic (7000 BCE to 2500 BCE) sites in South Asia, showing the development of early farming and pastoral societies.
 
• Archaeological evidence indicates the early use of pottery, tools, and domestication of animals.
 
• The site has provided crucial insights into the early stages of human settlement and the transition from nomadic to settled life.
 
• Excavations at Mehrgarh have revealed a rich cultural sequence, including burial practices, housing structures, and early craft activities.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**
 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization (IVC) flourished around 3300 BCE to 1300 BCE, with major urban centers like Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• It is known for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• The IVC is significant for its undeciphered script, standardized weights, and measures, and a complex drainage system.
 
• The civilization's decline around 1900 BCE is still a subject of research, with theories ranging from climate change to invasion.
 
 
 
• **Neolithic Revolution**
 
 
• The Neolithic Revolution, also known as the Agricultural Revolution, marked the transition from hunting and gathering to agriculture and settlement.
 
• This period saw the domestication of plants and animals, leading to the establishment of permanent settlements.
 
• The revolution began around 10,000 BCE in various parts of the world, including the Fertile Crescent, China, and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It led to significant changes in human societies, including population growth, social stratification, and technological advancements.
